Hello HeliumDeploy Team,

I have already purchased a Harlo B30 miner from your store, and I am currently preparing a dedicated ventilated rack cabinet for its installation.

Before purchasing the cabinet, I would appreciate your confirmation of a few technical details.

1. Exact dimensions and weight

Could you please provide the exact external dimensions of the complete Harlo B30 (width × height × depth, in millimetres), including any protruding components?

2. Airflow direction

Could you confirm the exact airflow direction?

* Do the rear-mounted fans draw cool air into the miner and exhaust hot air through the opposite side?

* Or do they extract hot air from the heatsink toward the rear?

3. Rack installation and ventilation

I am considering a 12U or 15U rack cabinet with a depth of 450 mm, featuring a perforated front door and ventilated side panels.

Could you please clarify:

* What minimum clearance should be maintained around the air intake and exhaust?

* Can the B30 safely operate rotated 90 degrees horizontally, with its intake and exhaust facing the rack's perforated side panels?

* Would you recommend this arrangement for continuous 24/7 operation?

* Are there any specific ventilation or ambient-temperature recommendations for installing the B30 inside a rack cabinet?

My goal is to ensure proper cooling, long-term reliability and safe operation without restricting airflow.

Thank you very much for your assistance.

Best regards

Hello Francesco,

Thanks for planning this properly before you buy the cabinet. I will be straight with you about what I can confirm today and what I will not guess at.

On the exact external dimensions in millimetres, including protrusions, and the unit weight: those figures are not published on our product page or in the Harlo material I can check, so I have asked JD, our hardware lead, to measure a unit and give you the real numbers rather than an estimate from me. The same goes for the airflow direction. The B30 is fan and heatsink cooled with the fans on the rear, but whether they push cool air in across the heatsink or pull hot air out of it is exactly the kind of detail you do not want me guessing at when you are sizing a cabinet, so JD confirms it. The team picks this up tomorrow from 10am Eastern and the answer comes to you as a reply in this thread. If you want it faster, JD is very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , and you can ask him directly there as @nullhashrate.

What I can tell you now is the thermal load you are designing around. In its default Turbo mode the B30 draws about 485 W at the wall, which comes out as roughly 1655 BTU per hour of heat into the cabinet. Balanced is about 350 W and ECO about 230 W, and both are a genuinely good option inside an enclosure: ECO is also the most efficient mode the machine has, at about 12.8 J/TH. Power comes from a 540 W supply built into the case with a standard IEC C14 inlet, so you need one C13 cord and one outlet per unit, nothing special. Network is 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi or RJ45 Ethernet, and in a metal cabinet I would strongly suggest Ethernet, because a closed steel enclosure will hurt Wi-Fi.

On the cabinet itself, the thing that kills miners in racks is not the miner, it is recirculation: hot exhaust finding its way back to the intake inside a closed box. A perforated front door and vented side panels are passive, and at 485 W of continuous heat passive venting alone is usually not enough in a sealed cabinet. I would add active extraction at the top or rear, sized so the cabinet pulls out clearly more air than the miner moves, and feed it cool air low at the front so the flow goes bottom front to top rear. Keep the intake air under about 30 C at the machine and aim to keep the cabinet rise over room temperature small, ideally under 10 C. Leave a generous gap at both intake and exhaust, at least 100 mm and more like 150 mm at the exhaust if you can, and never let either face sit flat against a panel or a door, perforated or not. A 450 mm deep cabinet is workable but tight once a power cord is plugged into the back, so plan the rear gap with the cord bend in mind.

On rotating it 90 degrees so intake and exhaust face the perforated side panels: thermally this kind of fan and heatsink design does not care much about gravity, and what matters is that neither face is blocked. That said, I would rather JD confirm the orientation for 24/7 operation than have me say yes from general principle, so I have included that question with the dimensions. One more thing worth knowing up front: opening or modifying the unit, including swapping fans, voids the warranty, and so does running it above its rated 30 TH/s. Inside a cabinet I would run Balanced or ECO anyway.

Your earlier point about the interview and the thank you compensation is still with the team and is not forgotten; that one is theirs to answer, not mine, and they pick it up tomorrow morning as well.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
I look forward to your kind response regarding the measurements.

Hello Francesco,

Just a short note so you are not left wondering: your request is with JD, our hardware lead, and he is the one measuring an actual unit for the external dimensions in millimetres, the weight and the confirmed airflow direction. Nothing more is needed from you. He comes online today at 10am Eastern and the figures will come to you as a reply in this thread.

If you would like them sooner, JD is usually quickest to answer on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , where he goes by @nullhashrate. Posting your question there often gets a reply within minutes, and other owners who have already racked a B30 may chime in with their own measurements.

In the meantime, the numbers I gave you for the cabinet sizing still hold, so you can keep working on the ventilation plan: about 485 W and roughly 1655 BTU per hour in Turbo, 350 W in Balanced, 230 W in ECO, one IEC C13 cord into the back, and active extraction out of the top or rear so no hot air loops back to the intake. If you hold off ordering the cabinet until the exact dimensions land, you lose nothing, and that is what I would do in your place.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hi Francesco,

Thanks for your patience, and sorry the Discord message went unanswered over the weekend. JD is back online today and I have pushed your request to the top of his list again this morning, with the three things you need spelled out: the exact external dimensions in millimetres including any protruding parts, the weight of the unit, and which face is intake and which is exhaust, plus his yes or no on running it rotated 90 degrees for 24/7 operation. The answer comes to you as a reply in this thread today. I am not going to invent numbers in the meantime, because a cabinet bought on a guess is an expensive mistake.

One thing that may unblock part of your order while you wait. The B30 is a desktop style box, not a 19 inch rack unit, so it has no rails or mounting ears and will sit on a shelf inside the cabinet. That means the cabinet choice itself is fairly forgiving if you pick adjustable shelves and leave yourself depth margin. With a 450 mm deep cabinet the tight dimension will be depth once the power cord is plugged in at the back, so a cord with an angled C13 connector is a cheap way to buy yourself 30 to 40 mm. Shelves, a top extraction fan and the cord are all things you can order now without the exact millimetres.

On the ventilation side nothing changes from what I sent you: plan for about 485 W of heat in Turbo, roughly 1655 BTU per hour, 350 W in Balanced and 230 W in ECO, intake air under about 30 C, and forced extraction at the top or rear so the exhaust cannot curl back round to the intake. In a closed cabinet I would run Balanced or ECO as a matter of course.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hello Francesco,

You are right to chase, and I am sorry. Three times is too many for a set of measurements. I have raised it again this morning and marked it as blocking a purchase you are waiting to make. The team is on from 10am Eastern today, which is 3pm in Italy, and the figures come to you as a reply in this thread. I have also said plainly that your Discord message went unanswered, so the reply should come by email rather than leaving you to chase there.

I will not fill the gap with invented numbers. A guessed depth or a guessed airflow direction is exactly what would make you buy the wrong cabinet, and that would be worse than waiting another few hours.

What I can do is make sure the wait costs you as little as possible. Since the B30 is a desktop box rather than a 19 inch rack unit, it will sit on a shelf and has no rails, so the cabinet itself is forgiving as long as you choose adjustable shelves and do not pick the shallowest model available. In a 450 mm deep cabinet the only genuinely tight dimension will be depth once the power cord is in, and an angled C13 cord recovers 30 to 40 mm of that. Shelves, the extraction fan and the angled cord can all be ordered now. The one decision I would hold back is the cabinet depth itself.

The thermal plan does not change with the measurements either, so that part of your design is safe: about 485 W and roughly 1655 BTU per hour in Turbo, 350 W in Balanced, 230 W in ECO, intake air under about 30 C, forced extraction out of the top or rear, and nothing solid directly in front of either face. In an enclosed cabinet I would run Balanced or ECO as standard.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
